item.title: Unemployment rate to rise in the coming months
item.description: 2,87% in the third quarter in Ticino 3,31% forecast in the fourth quarter 2026 3,45% estimated in the first quarter 2027 Youth rate rising: 5,7% Seco rate
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 2,87% in the third quarter in Ticino - 3,31% forecast for the fourth quarter of 2026 - 3,45% estimated for the first quarter of 2027 - Youth rate increasing: 5,7%
## Key facts - Seco unemployment rate in Ticino → 2,87% - Fourth quarter of 2026 → 3,31% - First quarter of 2027 → 3,45% - Swiss residents → 2,2% - Female unemployment → 2,77% - Male unemployment → 2,9% - Share of women among the unemployed → 44,5% - Youth unemployment → 5,7%
The 2,87% recorded in Ticino in the third quarter of the year is the starting point of the latest update on Seco unemployment forecasts in Ticino, released by the Institute of Economic Research of the University of Italian Switzerland (Ire). The institute expects the rate to increase from now until the end of the year and also at the beginning of 2027.
The Ire model places the rate at 3,31% in the fourth quarter of 2026 and at 3,45% in the first quarter of 2027. These are the two time windows indicated for the expected growth: the final part of the current year and the beginning of the following year. The forecast concerns the Seco rate in Ticino and is presented as an estimate from the Ire model.
### The third-quarter picture
In the third quarter, the cantonal rate reached 2,87%, 0,3 percentage points higher year on year. Among Swiss residents, the rate was 2,2%, while among foreigners the figure was 4,17. The increase compared with the same period of the previous year was 0,2 percentage points for the former and 0,5 for the latter.
The gender breakdown shows a female unemployment rate of 2,77% and a male rate of 2,9%. The share of women among all unemployed people rose to 44,5% compared with the previous period, although it was down compared with that of last year. The youth unemployment figure, on the other hand, increased compared with the previous year and stood at 5,7%.
Ire, through the forecasts prepared by O-De, the Observatory of Economic Dynamics, therefore continues to indicate growth for both periods considered. The Usi institute nevertheless accompanies the figures with an explicit note of caution:
> The Usi institute specifies that, despite the usual caution in interpretation, the latest figures would appear to be higher than those of the previous year.
For the cross-border worker who works in Ticino, the figure to follow is therefore the overall evolution of the cantonal rate over the two quarters indicated. The source does not add an individual forecast, but makes the expected direction of the regional labor market clear. For a cross-border worker, the update provides an indicator of the labor market in Canton Ticino, but not an individual decision. The source covers aggregate rates and a forecasting model; it does not indicate how many employment relationships will change, which professions will be involved, or which people will lose their jobs. This distinction avoids reading 3,31% or 3,45% as a personal forecast.
### Three comparisons to keep separate
The first comparison concerns residence. In the report, Swiss and foreign residents have different values and also different annual increases. For a cross-border worker, however, the source does not say that the figure for foreign residents automatically coincides with that for cross-border workers. That overlap is not contained in the update and should not be added to the interpretation.
The second comparison is between rate and composition. The female and male rates measure two distinct values; the 44,5% share, on the other hand, describes the presence of women among all unemployed people. It is therefore not a second female rate, but a composition indicator referring to the previous period and compared with that of last year.
The third comparison concerns young people. The 5,7% is accompanied by the indication that the rate increased compared with the previous year. The text does not cross-reference this figure with residence or gender: it therefore does not make it possible to derive a specific value for young foreign residents, women, or cross-border workers.
The text does not address the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates, INPS, or double taxation. Consequently, these elements cannot automatically be linked to the Ire forecast: the bulletin does not indicate changes in taxation, social security, health insurance, or procedures for cross-border workers.
The time comparison remains. The estimates for the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027 signal an expected direction, accompanied by the institute’s caution. For those who work in Ticino, they are therefore a reference for the general trend in unemployment, not a calculation of their own employment risk. To follow the figure without attributing more meaning to it than is contained in the source, a cross-border worker can use a brief reading procedure. The aim is to distinguish the observed figure, future estimates and the categories used by Ire.
### Four steps
1. Start with the period observed. Record the third quarter as the basis for comparison and note the 2,87% Seco rate in Ticino. Keep this value separate from the two future estimates.
2. Separate residence. Report 2,2% for Swiss residents and 4,17 for foreign residents, together with the annual increases of 0,2 and 0,5 percentage points. Do not combine the two indicators into a single figure.
3. Keep gender, composition and age distinct. The values 2,77% and 2,9% are the female and male rates; 44,5% is the share of women among the total unemployed; 5,7% is the youth rate. They are different lines in the reading.
4. Place the two estimates on the calendar: 3,31% for the fourth quarter 2026 and 3,45% for the first quarter 2027. Next to both, note that Ire recommends caution and identifies them as values higher than those of the previous year.
This method prevents using a cantonal forecast as if it were the result of a single position and confusing a rate with a share of the total. The source allows comparison between the periods and groups indicated, but not a personal calculation.
If the question concerns the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, rebates, INPS or double taxation, this source does not provide data, deadlines, documents, rates or operational steps on these topics. It is therefore not possible to derive an administrative procedure for the cross-border worker from Ire’s figures.
To follow the topic, consult section Disoccupazione frontalieri.
*Source: [laregione.ch](https://www.laregione.ch/cantone/ticino/1956748/tasso-di-disoccupazione-in-crescita-nei-prossimi-mesi)*

item.title: Migros: new CCL from 2027, 10% discount
item.description: Migros’ national CCL will be in force from 2027 to 2031: uniform conditions, a 41-hour workweek for many, and a 10% discount with shopping vouchers.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - National CCL in force from 2027 to 2031 - 10% discount with shopping vouchers - Same conditions even below 20% employment - After 90 days: 80% of gross salary
## Key facts - Duration → 2027-2031 - Purchases → 10% discount with shopping vouchers - Employment → same conditions even below 20% - Working hours → 41 hours instead of 43 for many employees - Illness or accident → full net pay for 90 days, then 80% of gross pay
From 2027 to 2031, the new national collective labor agreement for Migros will be in force. The company indicates better conditions for employees, with measures concerning shopping, working hours, and payment in the event of illness or accident.
The most immediate benefit concerns purchases: employees will be able to shop with a 10% discount through shopping vouchers. The source does not specify an amount for the vouchers, nor does it describe the procedure by which they will be distributed or used. The verifiable information is therefore the discount percentage and its connection to the shopping vouchers.
The CCL will apply regardless of the employment percentage. Those working at a percentage below 20% will also benefit from the same conditions. For a cross-border worker employed by Migros, this is the part to read most carefully in their employment relationship: the criterion indicated is the employment percentage, not a different threshold described in the text.
### Working hours and income protection
Regarding working hours, the company emphasizes that many employees will move to 41 hours per week instead of 43, while maintaining the same salary. The wording concerns many employees, does not establish that the reduction applies to everyone, and does not indicate which positions are included.
Benefits in the event of illness or accident will also be uniform. Full net salary will be paid for a maximum of 90 days; subsequently, 80% of gross salary will be paid. The distinction between net and gross is an essential part of the measure: the text does not permit converting 80% gross into a net figure or extending the first period beyond 90 days.
When reading the payslip, the source therefore provides two different and consecutive references: net pay for the first phase and gross pay for the subsequent one. No absolute amount is indicated, and it is not explained how the employer will operationally implement the transition; these elements remain outside the available text.
The connection with cross-border work remains limited to the employment conditions at Migros. The source does not indicate locations, employee numbers, or specific details for Canton Ticino: it presents the CCL as national and sets its validity from 2027 to 2031. ## How to read the change as a cross-border worker
For a cross-border worker employed by Migros, the new CCL should be read as a change to the employment conditions, not as information about all aspects of cross-border work. The source limits the changes to four elements: discount on purchases, employment level, weekly hours, and benefits in the event of sickness or an accident.
### The practical comparison
| Item | Indication of the new CCL | |---|---| | Purchases | 10% discount via shopping vouchers | | Employment level | same conditions even below 20% | | Hours | 41 hours instead of 43 for many employees, with the same salary | | Sickness or accident | full net salary for up to 90 days, then 80% of gross salary |
The table helps avoid confusing different measures. The 10% concerns purchases and is linked to shopping vouchers; the text does not describe it in other terms. The 20% threshold concerns the application of the CCL conditions, and the source does not add any other thresholds. The change from 43 to 41 hours applies to many employees, while the salary remains the same for those covered by the measure indicated by the company.
The section on absences also requires a separate reading. During the first period, the reference is the full net salary, with a maximum limit of 90 days. After that limit, the reference changes: 80% is calculated on the gross salary, according to the source's wording. Without an individual salary figure, the text makes it possible to clarify the rule, but not to calculate a personal amount.
To avoid overinterpretation, the scope must be kept narrow. The source does not mention a G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates, or double taxation. These matters therefore cannot be presented as having been changed by the CCL described.
For the cross-border worker, the useful information is the separation between the contractual level and other topics: here, the subject is the conditions offered by Migros to employees, without additional information on taxation, social security, health insurance, or commuting. ## Checklist for the 2027-2031 period
A Migros cross-border employee can turn the information in the CCL into a simple check, without adding data not provided by the text. The objective is to distinguish what is already defined from what remains to be specified.
### Five practical checks
1. Check the percentage of work. If the percentage is below 20%, the new CCL indicates access to the same conditions. The relevant reference is that of the employment relationship. 2. Compare the weekly hours. Check whether the position is among those of the many employees for whom 41 hours rather than 43 are indicated. The comparison must keep the corresponding salary data alongside it. 3. Separate out the shopping benefit. Record that the discount is 10% and that the source links it to shopping vouchers. The text does not indicate amounts, delivery methods or the duration of the vouchers, so these details should not be reconstructed. 4. Note the two phases in the event of absence. In the event of illness or accident, the first reference is the full net salary for a maximum of 90 days. After that, 80% of the gross salary applies. Keeping the two references separate avoids comparing net and gross as if they were the same item. 5. Note the time window. The CCL will be in force from 2027 to 2031, but the source does not indicate the precise start day or an individual procedure. The certain data to use is therefore the stated interval, not an invented calendar deadline.
This checklist does not expand the content of the agreement. The source does not link the measures to external tax or social-security matters and does not describe individual procedures for employees. For the cross-border reader, the check thus remains anchored to the working conditions indicated by Migros.
After collecting the percentage, hours and salary references, you can organize the comparison between gross and net with simulatore busta paga.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4164916)*

The match ended with an 82-85 defeat, but the most significant update for the red and white club concerns the player's condition.

This point is relevant because the club describes a team called upon to continue its campaign in the league and cup while having to do without a player who represents a reference point in its tactical structure. This is the red-and-white side's situation as it relates to the absence.
This is the sporting impact highlighted by the club: Della Valle is mentioned not only for his presence on the court, but for the role he plays in the tactical setup and as the team's offensive focal point. ## What follows: check-ups and live broadcast

The next step on the sporting and medical front is the monitoring indicated by Pallacanestro Varese. item.title: Tre Valli: 80 operators in four exercises
item.description: Around 80 operators trained in 2026 Four editions between Biasca and Giornico Three scenarios: fire, public order and bad weather Training will continue
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - About 80 operators trained in 2026 - Four editions between Biasca and Giornico - Three scenarios: fire, public order and bad weather - Training will continue in another region
## Key facts - Participants → approximately 80 operators - Year → 2026 - Editions → four - Locations → Biasca and Giornico - Scenarios → fire, public order and bad weather
### The course and its objectives
In 2026, approximately 80 operators took part in four editions of the course for the command staff of first-response organizations, referred to by the acronym SMEPI. Organized between Biasca and Giornico, the sessions were overseen by the Technical Commission for Training in Civil Protection.
The course was designed to improve the management of emergencies requiring the coordinated intervention of multiple services. It did not involve responses to real events: the activities used simulated scenarios to develop the ability to assess situations, make operational decisions and activate responses.
### The three scenarios
The exercises tested participants in three situations. The first concerned a fire at the Heavy Vehicle Control Centre in Giornico. The second reproduced a public-order incident at the Industrial Services Centre of the Ente Ospedaliero Cantonale (EOC), in Biasca. The third was a weather-related emergency at Casa anziani leventinese in Giornico.
The work was led by instructors and carried out with the support of the managers of the infrastructures involved. In this way, participants were able to operate in their respective roles and apply the common procedures established through coordination between organizations.
Participants included heads of police, fire brigades and ambulance services, as well as Civil Protection officers and specialists from the Cantonal Technical Services. SMEPI serve as coordination structures where the organizations involved jointly organize the response to an emergency.
The program does not end with the four 2026 editions. An additional phase is planned for next year in another region of the canton, with different scenarios and new participants. The aim is to strengthen preparedness and cooperation among the organizations called upon to respond in crisis situations. ### A territorial, not tax-related connection
For a cross-border worker who works in Canton Ticino, this is not news about the G permit, AVS, LPP or LAMal: the source deals solely with training for emergency response. The connection is territorial and concerns the presence of coordinated activities between Biasca and Giornico. However, there are no elements to assert that the course led to changes in traffic conditions, schedules, access or services for the public.
Anyone crossing the border to work therefore finds information about how first-response organizations operate, not an operational notice. The source does not indicate which routes should be avoided, whether detours are planned or whether the scenarios had consequences for travel times. Nor does it describe communications addressed to workers or users of the infrastructure involved.
### What can and cannot be inferred
The content does not concern the G permit, AVS, LPP or LAMal. It does not describe working conditions, pay slips, pensions or health insurance. Introducing these topics would mean attributing to the training an effect that the source does not report.
For the same reason, it is not possible to turn the number of about 80 operators into an estimate of the people involved in a possible real event. The figure concerns participation in the course, not the size of a team on duty or its presence in the area. The future perspective is also precise: next year, new scenarios and additional participants are announced in another region of the canton, but the location, schedule or composition are not indicated.
The practical value, for those who work in Ticino, is therefore the distinction between organizational preparedness and travel or work guidance. The former is documented; the latter are not contained in the text. ### A four-step reading guide
1. Separate simulation and news reporting. The text presents the episodes as simulated scenarios. The first step therefore consists in not treating fire, public order and bad weather as reports of an ongoing emergency.
2. Separate location and impact. Biasca and Giornico are the locations indicated for the course and for the infrastructure involved. However, the source does not communicate closures, diversions, travel times, access or instructions for those traveling. These elements cannot be inferred from the article.
3. Separate roles and recipients. The training concerns the command staffs of first-response agencies and the exercise of common procedures. No individual procedure for users, workers or cross-border commuters is described; the text explains coordination among agencies.
4. Mark the next point of verification. The training activity is expected to resume in another region of the canton, with new scenarios and the involvement of other participants. The report does not yet indicate the venue, schedule, documents or participation methods.
For those who work across the border, this sequence avoids reading more into the news than it allows. The usable fact is the existence of a preparation program and its announced continuation. No new rules for travel or work emerge, however. The figure of about 80 operators must also be maintained in its precise meaning: participants in the four editions of the course, not a general measure of the response available.
In the absence of other indications in the text, the correct action is to stop at the locations, the simulated scenarios, the roles involved and the next announced development.

item.title: Bellinzona: vote on funding for the new barracks
item.description: On Monday, the first credit of 14 million will be put to a vote.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - On Monday, the first credit of 14 million will be put to a vote. - The ex LATI project is estimated at 34 million. - The minority is calling for the ex LATI option to be rejected. - A referendum has already been announced.
## Key facts - Decision → initial credit for the land and the project for the new fire station - Initial amount → 14 million - Overall operation → estimated at 34 million - Proposed site → former LATI site in Sant'Antonino - Alternative → former Birreria in Carasso, approximately 44 million - Reports → majority in favor, minority opposed - Entities brought together → firefighters, Civil Protection and the City's operational services - Referendum → announced by anonymous firefighters and the MPS of Bellinzona
On Monday, the Bellinzona City Council will vote on an initial credit of 14 million. The financing is intended to acquire the former LATI site in Sant'Antonino and design the new fire station. The overall operation is estimated at 34 million.
The solution is supported by the majority report of the Management Commission. President Pietro Ghisletta considers the former LATI site an interesting area, located in an industrial zone with considerable development potential remaining. The project would also make it possible to bring the firefighters, Civil Protection and the entire operational services sector of the City of Bellinzona under one roof. According to Ghisletta, travel times have also been analyzed and are considered suitable.
### The NoCasa committee's letter
The vote comes after intense months and just days after a new letter sent to the municipal councillors by a group of firefighters gathered in the NoCasa committee. The signatories remain anonymous for fear of repercussions and declare themselves opposed to moving the station to the former LATI site.
> «We hope that none of you will be influenced by party interests or directives imposed from above».
The opposing side is also represented by a minority report, which calls for rejecting the option. Among the signatories is Brenno Martignoni Polti, according to whom a station tasked with covering a territory must guarantee rapid response and cannot accept situations that are still unclear. The Noce representative points to the significant traffic linked to the nearby shopping center and argues that there is currently no certainty that the existing rescue capabilities can be maintained.
Some opponents would have preferred the former Birreria in Carasso, an option already mooted decades ago. However, the Municipal Council considers it more expensive, with an estimate of approximately 44 million. Ghisletta explained that the Management Commission met with the firefighters' representatives, including Tuto Rossi and Rodolfo Quatraccioni, and also heard from Civil Protection several times. ## In brief - Two arrests in Varese for family abuse - The first incident occurred Saturday afternoon - Five minor children were present, aged between 5 and 8 years - The second intervention took place Sunday morning
## Key facts - Force involved → Operational unit and mobile unit of Varese - Offences → abuse against family members or cohabitants - First arrested → 52‑year‑old man - Second arrested → 36‑year‑old man - Procedure → Red Code
### Saturday's episode
During the weekend in Varese, the Carabinieri of the Operational unit and mobile unit intervened in two distinct episodes attributable to abuse against family members or cohabitants. The outcome of the interventions is two arrests in the act of committing a crime, both within the framework of the Red Code. The two episodes required the immediate intervention of the troops.
In the city centre, on Saturday afternoon, the 52‑year‑old, already known to law‑enforcement, reached the former wife’s workplace. There he began to shout at her and hurl heavy insults, while the five minor children of the couple were present on site, all aged between 5 and 8 years.
The episode took place at the former wife’s workplace, in the city centre, in front of the five minor children of the couple, all aged between 5 and 8 years. The timely intervention of the Carabinieri led to the man’s detention and arrest in the act, within the Red Code.
The second episode, separate from the first, occurred on Sunday morning and involved a 36‑year‑old man. This intervention was also carried out by the Carabinieri of the Operational unit and mobile unit of Varese. The distinction between the two moments of the weekend is clear: Saturday afternoon in the city centre, Sunday morning at the elderly parents’ home. The details of the raid and the man’s conduct constitute the continuation of the reconstruction. ### The break-in at the parents' home
Sunday morning was marked by the second intervention by the Carabinieri from Varese's Operational and Radio-Mobile Unit. At the center of the incident was a 36-year-old unemployed, homeless man who had forced his way into his elderly parents' home. The front door was damaged during the break-in.
The account of the incident describes the man as being in an evidently altered mental and physical state. Once inside the house, he allegedly behaved aggressively and refused to leave the home. Faced with this situation, the officers detained him. This incident, too, resulted in an arrest in flagrante delicto for abuse against family members or cohabitants.
| Element | Reported data | |---|---| | Time | Sunday morning | | Person detained | 36-year-old unemployed, homeless man | | Location | Elderly parents' home | | Damage | Front door damaged | | Conduct described | Aggressive behavior and refusal to leave the house |

The behavior displayed once he entered the house is reported using the conditional mood, while the altered mental and physical state and the subsequent detention form part of the reconstruction of the intervention.
As with the other incident, the emergency procedure provided for under the Red Code was already in place. In the text, this procedure is linked to the protection of victims of domestic and gender-based violence and governs interventions in the cases indicated. Although the two arrests took place at different times and in different homes, they fall within the same operational framework for responding to family-related offenses. ### From confirmation to measures
Once the required formalities had been completed, the two arrested individuals were taken to the Varese detention facility. The arrests were then confirmed and resulted in different measures: one was ordered to remain in prison, while the other was prohibited from approaching the injured party, with an electronic monitoring bracelet applied.
Following confirmation, therefore, what happened next was different: imprisonment on one hand and a restraining order accompanied by an electronic monitoring bracelet on the other. The bracelet was applied together with the restraining order, as reported in the account of the interventions. The transfer to the Varese detention facility, on the other hand, had taken place for both after the customary formalities.
In both cases, the Carabinieri of the Varese Operational and Radiomobile Unit intervened when the urgent procedure under the Red Code had already been activated. It is intended to regulate interventions to protect victims of domestic and gender-based violence.
The final crime report included two arrests carried out over the weekend, the subsequent transfer to the detention facility, and two different decisions following confirmation. What happened falls within the Carabinieri’s daily commitment to preventing and combating crimes in the family sphere. Following confirmation, the measures provided for imprisonment for one of the two and a restraining order with an electronic monitoring bracelet for the other.

## TL;DR - Network nearing completion in 145 municipalities in the province of Como - More than 27,9 million in public funds for Como - Ultra-broadband take-up: 23% versus 17% - Italia 1 Giga Plan completed in 50 municipalities
## Key facts - Projects → «Bul Announcement – Ultra Broadband» and «Italy 1 Giga Plan» - Province of Como → over 27.9 million in public resources - Regional contribution → 7.4 million euros - Bul Plan → 145 municipalities and just over 144,000 real estate units - Italy 1 Giga Plan → 50 municipalities and over 12,700 civics - Adherence → 23% compared to 17% of the national average - White areas in Lombardy → 1,429 Municipalities and 261 million in public funds - Technology → FTTH, fiber to the home
## Provincial works and network nearing completion
### The picture communicated to Como
The meeting held in Como marked the completion of the laying of optical fiber in the entire province. The interventions are part of the public projects «Bando Bul – Ultra Broadband» and «Piano Italia 1 Giga». Franco Lucente, Councilor for Transport and Sustainable Mobility of the Lombardy Region, spoke via video link.
The passage across the 145 municipalities requires precision: the source indicates that Open Fiber is completing the ultra-broadband network envisaged by the Bul Plan. It is therefore not described as already completed in all the municipalities involved. The connected real estate units are just over 144,000 and for these it is possible to request the activation of the service.
The status indicated for the Italy 1 Giga Plan is different. Open Fiber has completed interventions in 50 municipalities in Como; There are over 12,700 civic addresses where it is possible to request activation. The program concerns gray areas, while the Bul Plan affects white areas, i.e. rural and peripheral areas where there is no private interest in investing.
The meeting served to share the results, illustrate the opportunities for the municipalities involved and collect observations and critical issues from local administrators. Lucente indicated that ultra-broadband supports the economic and social growth of the province, especially in areas not covered by private investments. In the Como area, the level of participation in ultra-broadband services is 23%, compared to a national average of 17%.
The interventions in the white areas involved 1,429 Lombardy municipalities, with 261 million in public funds, of which 70 million regional. In the province of Como, public resources exceed 27.9 million euros, with a contribution from the Lombardy Region amounting to 7.4 million. Massimiliano Vari, Marco Luttati, Daniele Mariuzzo and Sergio Galli also participated in the meeting. ## The difference between white areas and gray areas
### Two programs not to be confused
The Bul Plan and the Italia 1 Giga Plan address two different infrastructure situations. White areas are rural and peripheral zones in which there is no private interest in investing. Gray areas, on the other hand, are those where the private operator has no interest in using its own funds to enhance connectivity up to 1 Gbps. In both cases, the intervention is public, but the scope does not coincide.

The press release does not indicate forms, documents, portals, fees or timelines for the request. It is therefore possible to define only a verification sequence based on the available data, without adding procedures not described.

item.title: ASVZ Blackbirds win Champions Bowl: first Swiss European title in flag football
item.description: The ASVZ Blackbirds triumph at the 2026 Champions Bowl, winning the first historic European flag football title for a Swiss team.
item.content:encoded:
The ASVZ Blackbirds of Zurich won the Champions Bowl 2026, the leading European tournament for flag football clubs. It is the first success of a Swiss team in the competition. The final, played on October 11 in Poreč, Croatia, ended 46-14 against Molosses Flag Asnières, a team from the Paris region.
The tournament ran from October 9-11 and the Blackbirds were unbeaten. After finishing in first place in both group stages, the Zurich team beat the Kranjski Jazbeci, from Slovenia, and the Italian Parma Panthers in the quarterfinals.
In the end, the Blackbirds' defense intercepted six passes: two apiece for Claudio Ferrari and for the brothers Justin and Oliver Verhoek. Attacking quarterback Dennis Sieger threw six touchdowns and scored another on the run; Frédéric Eppisser received four of the touchdown passes. The Blackbirds also conceded fewer points than all other teams in the men's competition.
"This title is the reward for years of hard work. When we founded the club, almost ten years ago, we would not have dared to dream of such a result, "said player-coach Fabiano Piccinno. "In the final we played an almost perfect game. I'm incredibly proud of this team. ” For the ASVZ Blackbirds it is the eighth participation in the Champions Bowl. In 2024 they finished in second place and in 2025 in third. The club, founded in 2017, also won six national titles and also won the shortened Covid season, played without an official championship.
The result comes on the eve of flag football's Olympic debut in Los Angeles 2028. The non-contact discipline will be part of the Olympic programme for the first time.

## TL;DR
- October 12, 2026: checks at a construction site in Lurate Caccivio - Inspection by the Carabinieri of Como and the Labor Inspectorate - Deficiencies found concerning the POS, ladders, protective measures and internal traffic - Operations suspended and administrative fines of 5.500 euro
## Key facts
- Date: October 12, 2026 - Location: Lurate Caccivio - Authorities: Carabinieri of the Como Labor Inspectorate Unit and Territorial Labor Inspectorate - Plan: extraordinary inspections on health and safety at construction sites - Outcome: referral to the authorities without arrest and immediate suspension of operations - Sanctions: additional 5.500 euro
### Inspections in the Como area
A construction site in Lurate Caccivio was inspected on October 12, 2026, by the Carabinieri of the Como Labor Inspectorate Unit, assisted by the Territorial Labor Inspectorate. The morning saw inspections and sanctions in the Como area, with the operation focused on the site's safety conditions.
The operation is part of the extraordinary inspection plan devoted to preventing workplace accidents and ensuring compliance with health and safety regulations at construction sites. The plan referred to in the report therefore has two objectives: preventing accidents and ensuring the application of safety rules in places where construction work is carried out.
The inspection involved the Carabinieri of the Como Labor Inspectorate Unit and the Territorial Labor Inspectorate. During the operation, law enforcement officers and inspectors found deficiencies both in the site's structure and in the required paperwork.
The inspection thus initiated the investigations that led to the subsequent measures. The construction site inspected is located in Lurate Caccivio, and the operation was carried out as part of the extraordinary inspections into safety at construction sites. ## The irregularities identified
### Documents, protective measures and traffic routes
The inspection brought to light a set of problems that the report places in two areas: structural and bureaucratic issues. It was not just the documentation that was challenged, because the inspectors and the Carabinieri also recorded conditions related to protective measures and the organization of internal spaces.
From a bureaucratic standpoint, the construction site lacked the POS, that is, the Operational Safety Plan. In terms of accident prevention, however, adequate protection against falls from height was found to be absent. These are the two findings listed along with the other deficiencies identified during the inspection.
A further issue concerned the ladders, which were found not to comply with safety rules. Internal traffic within the construction site was also deemed irregular and dangerous. The findings therefore concern documents, protective measures, ladders and movement arrangements within the work area.
The violations were attributed to accident-prevention legislation. In the report, the lack of the POS, the absence of protection against falls, non-compliant ladders and irregular internal traffic make up the picture of the serious irregularities identified at the construction site in Lurate Caccivio. These are the safety deficiencies identified following the inspection conducted by law enforcement and the inspectors. ## Report and suspension
### The consequences of the inspection
The sole director of the company carrying out the work was reported by the Carabinieri without being detained: he is 59 years old, is of Argentine origin and resides in Lurate Caccivio.
For the company, however, measures directly related to the construction site's activities were imposed. The first is the immediate suspension of the work because of the serious safety deficiencies identified during the inspection. The second consists of administrative fines for a further 5.500 euro.
The measure described therefore includes a report against the sole director, who was not detained, and two consequences for the company: the immediate stoppage of operations and administrative fines. The link to the findings is explicit: the suspension was ordered because of the serious safety deficiencies that emerged at the construction site.
According to the report, the intervention confirms the utmost attention of the local authorities to protecting workers and preventing risks in construction settings. The documented outcome following the checks is therefore the suspension of operations, together with the report against the director and the additional administrative amount specified for the company.

item.title: Ticino cantonal deficit expected to reach 460 million
item.description: The 2027 budget forecasts a deficit of 98,5 million.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The 2027 Budget projects a deficit of 98,5 million. - The projected deficit reaches 460 million in 2030. - From 2028, self-financing is expected to become negative. - Mirante and the co-signatories are calling for a plan before the end of the legislative term.
## Key facts - 2027 Budget → operating deficit of 98,5 million francs - 2028-2030 Financial plan → 236 million in 2028, 411 in 2029, 460 in 2030 - Measures in the 2027 Budget → approximately 237 million francs - Spending review → cost differential of approximately 96,7 million - Interpellation → Amalia Mirante, Giovanni Albertini and Evaristo Roncelli - BAK Economics study → presented in December 2025 - Two motions → November 2025, still unanswered
## The financial picture The Canton’s 2027 Budget projects an operating deficit of 98,5 million francs.
It is this trajectory that forms the backdrop to the interpellation submitted by Amalia Mirante together with Giovanni Albertini and Evaristo Roncelli, of Avanti con Ticino&Lavoro. In the text, the signatories urge the Council of State to clarify which measures have already been developed and why they have not yet reached Parliament.
> “Why, in the face of these prospects, is the Government postponing the multi-year rebalancing plan until the beginning of the next legislative term?”
According to the interpellants, a substantial share of the deterioration could be attributed to factors already known. Among these, they cite the launch of EFAS, initiatives related to health insurance premiums, Confederation savings, the abolition of imputed rental value and the future introduction of individual taxation. In their view, this entire set of factors should have called for advance planning.
The 2027 Budget sets out measures amounting to approximately 237 million francs. Some of them, however, are based on extraordinary or temporary operations: the sale of assets, recourse to funds and reserves, and increased contributions from companies with government holdings. The interpellation argues that such solutions cannot replace a structural review of public spending.
### The spending review remains central The spending review also features among the interpellation’s topics. The time elapsed since the November 2023 motion is now close to three years, while the time since the Grand Council approved the legislative decree exceeds two; according to the signatories, an overall plan, accompanied by financial targets and defined deadlines, is still not available. Presented in December 2025, the BAK Economics study had identified a cost gap of approximately 96,7 million compared with comparable Cantons, but that figure does not automatically translate into achievable savings.
The final questions also concern the effects the postponement could have on indebtedness, public services and the finances of municipalities. As for revenues, the signatories ask whether measures such as raising the cantonal multiplier, changing exemption thresholds or adjusting the rates applied to married couples and families have been examined. The document finally mentions two motions from November 2025 that have not yet received a response, concerning the financing of initiatives on health insurance premiums and the concrete implementation of the initiative for 10%. ## What remains open for those who work in Ticino ### The hypotheses are not decisions For the cross-border worker working in Ticino, the news has a clearly defined scope: the source describes a political debate over the cantonal accounts and possible rebalancing choices. It does not present a measure already applied to cross-border taxation, permits or social benefits.
The text does not mention changes to the G permit, withholding tax, AVS, LPP or LAMal. Nor does it address tax rebates, double taxation, Brogeda, INPS or a new 2026 tax agreement. For this reason, it is not possible to derive from the source an amount for a cross-border worker's paycheck, a new deadline or a procedure to follow.
The practical point is different: the interpellation asks the Council of State to clarify what consequences the postponement could have for indebtedness, public services and municipalities' finances. These are areas the reader can follow, but without turning the signatories' questions into decisions already adopted.
| Area | Element mentioned | Status described in the source | | Revenue | Cantonal multiplier, exemption thresholds, tax rates for spouses and families | Hypotheses submitted to the Government | | Expenditure | Sale of assets, funds and reserves, contributions from companies in which the public sector holds stakes | Extraordinary or temporary solutions | | Fiscal consolidation | Options, financial impact and implementation timelines | Document still requested by the signatories |
The distinction matters because the possible increase in the multiplier, the change to the thresholds or the revision of the tax rates are not announced as measures. They are questions addressed to the Government. The same applies to the multi-year plan: the political request is that it be presented before the end of the legislative term, whereas the contested postponement would place it at the beginning of the subsequent legislative term.
On the spending side too, according to the interpellation, there is no comprehensive program with financial objectives and precise deadlines. The cost differential identified by BAK Economics can therefore serve as a point of comparison, but the source makes clear that it does not automatically equate to an achievable saving. For the cross-border worker, the conclusion is simple: today the dossier points to possible future choices, but it does not yet quantify their individual impact. ## How to follow the dossier ### A four-step review First: start from the two financial references cited in the source, the 2027 Budget and the 2028-2030 Financial Plan. The comparison must separate the operating deficit from subsequent projections and keep self-financing distinct, which is indicated as set to become negative from 2028.
Second: examine the composition of the measures envisaged in the 2027 Budget. The useful check consists in distinguishing what derives from the sale of capital assets, funds and reserves, or increased contributions from companies with public holdings, from structural spending review measures. It is precisely this difference on which the signatories base part of their criticism.
Third: verify whether the State Council will present the requested document before the end of the legislative term. The political request is that the document clarify which consolidation measures are feasible, what effects they would have on the accounts and when they could be implemented. Without a complete picture, a series of questions will remain open.
Fourth: follow the spending review and the two motions of November 2025 separately. For the first, the source refers to the motion of November 2023, the legislative decree approved by the Grand Council and the BAK Economics study of December 2025. For the latter, it will be necessary to check when the answers will arrive on how to finance the initiatives for health-insurance premiums and how to implement the initiative for 10%.
This sequence allows the cross-border worker not to automatically attribute effects on the G permit, withholding tax, AVS, LPP, LAMal, revenue-sharing payments or double taxation to the cantonal accounts: the source does not formulate decisions in these areas. Any consequences can be assessed only once the measures, amounts and deadlines are known.
When concrete assumptions about revenues become available, their tax effect can be estimated with calcolatore fiscale.

item.description: Two stops at Como after resident reports A forced car and a second vehicle damaged A motorist reports an injury to an arm

## In brief - Two arrests in Como following reports from residents - A car broken into and a second vehicle damaged - A motorist reports an arm injury - Charged with aggravated theft, attempted robbery, threats, and criminal damage
## Key facts - Location → via Dei Mulini and Val Mulini parking garage - Time → around 6:30 AM - Arrested → a 21-year-old Tunisian man and a 19-year-old Italian woman - Charges → jointly committed aggravated theft, attempted robbery, threats, and criminal damage
Around 6:30 AM, in via Dei Mulini in Como, the State Police intervened following reports from several residents. Some had heard loud noises and shouting coming from the street and had notified the police headquarters' operations center. A patrol from the 'Squadra Volante' reached the area in front of the Val Mulini parking garage, where they tracked down and stopped a 21-year-old Tunisian man and a 19-year-old Italian woman.
### Reconstruction in the parking lot According to what residents told the officers, the two young people allegedly entered the parking lot and broke into a parked car. After forcing the vehicle open, they reportedly rummaged through its interior. The owner allegedly asked them to leave. The two, again according to the reconstruction reported to the police, allegedly continued and directed threatening remarks at her.
In the same area, another resident went down to the street to check his parked vehicle. He found that part of the door and a window had been damaged. This damage was also reported to the officers during the patrol's intervention, which had been initiated due to the noises and shouting reported shortly before.
The first phase of the event took place between the parking lot and the area in front of Val Mulini. The two young people were detained there before being transferred to the Police Headquarters for further investigation. The reconstruction gathered by the officers concerned both the broken-into car and the second damaged vehicle. ## The Driver's Tale
### The attempt on the road During the intervention, another driver approached the Flying Team patrol. He told the agents that, shortly before, the two young men had stopped him while he was walking along Dei Mulini street and had threatened him. His story added to the scene of the parked vehicles an episode that took place along the same road, with the direct involvement of those behind the wheel.
According to the man, the 21-year-old allegedly injured him in the arm. The 19-year-old, on the other hand, allegedly tried to take a suitcase with work tools from the trunk. The victim reacted and retrieved the briefcase, then drove away. The sequence described to the agents then ended with the driver again in possession of the tools and away from the point where he would have been stopped.
The testimony came while the patrol was carrying out the intervention in the Val Mulini car park area. The driver spoke directly to the officers and placed the block just before they arrived. The story concerned both the threats addressed to the driver and the attempt to take the tools from the trunk; the wound indicated by the man was on one arm.
### The positions of the two stops During the investigations it emerged that the 21-year-old is a Tunisian citizen, resides in Olgiate Comasco and was found to be irregular on the national territory. The 19-year-old is Italian and resides in Carlazzo.
Both, according to the police, are homeless. The source also reports that they have several precedents for crimes against person and property. These elements were indicated after the stop in the Val Mulini area and the subsequent accompaniment in the Police Headquarters. ## From the police station to the prison
### Araştırma sonuçları: After stopping in the area in front of the Val Mulini car park, the 21-year-old and the 19-year-old were escorted to the police station. The State Police has indicated this step as the phase of the investigations following the intervention in Via Dei Mulini. The sequence shown distinguishes the first stop from the stop made at the end of the checks.
At the end of the investigations, in fact, the two young men were arrested. The complaints indicated are aggravated theft in competition, attempted robbery, threats and damage. These are the qualifications reported by the police for the facts reconstructed in the morning, after the reports of the residents and the story of the driver. The transfer to the Police Headquarters is therefore distinguished, in the chronology reported, from the arrest and the subsequent transfer to the Bassone.
### The destination indicated The next step was the transfer to the Bassone prison. The source states that both were taken to the facility available to the judicial authority. The prison destination is therefore the latest development reported after detention and investigations.
The scan described is linear: the Police Headquarters receives the reports, the Flying Team reaches via Dei Mulini, the two are stopped in the car park area, then accompanied to the Police Headquarters and finally arrested. Only after this sequence are they taken to the Bassone. Each step is referred to the same morning as the intervention of the State Police in Como.
The judicial outcome indicated by the source remains that of availability to the judicial authority. In the text, the documented follow-up after the arrest is the transfer of the two to the Bassone prison, at the disposal of the judicial authority.

## TL;DR - Sunday, October 18: ribbon-cutting at 11 a.m. - The former Regia Dogana is on Via Mazzini - The building becomes the new Tourist Office - Restoration supported by Regione Lombardia and Autorità di Bacino Lacuale
## Key facts - What: former Regia Dogana di Porto Ceresio - When: Sunday, October 18, at 11 a.m. - Where: Via Mazzini, opposite the railway station - Plan: Nuovo Baricentro Ceresino - Opening: event open to all residents
On Sunday, October 18, at 11 a.m., Porto Ceresio will inaugurate the former Regia Dogana on Via Mazzini, the historic building located directly opposite the railway station. The ribbon-cutting ceremony will accompany the reopening to the public of a fully restored site destined to become the town’s new Tourist Office.
The restoration has returned to the local community a building of architectural and cultural significance. The project was made possible by financial support from Regione Lombardia and the Autorità di Bacino Lacuale. The funding made it possible to protect and repurpose one of the most distinctive views on the Italian shore of the lake, preserving both the building’s historical dimension and its new public use.
### Redevelopment with a specific service The site is located in a strategic position for arrivals. Opposite the station, the Tourist Office will provide a first point of welcome, guidance and information for those reaching Porto Ceresio by train and for those visiting the lakeside village. Those using mezzi pubblici will therefore find the station to be the designated reference point for locating the new site.
The function described by the source is twofold: enhancing a restored building and giving the town a recognizable place for visitors and tourists. The project is not limited to preserving the historic appearance, but involves repurposing the building through a service aimed at the public.
The project is part of the urban development plan called «Nuovo Baricentro Ceresino». The strategy concerns this specific area of Porto Ceresio and aims to redesign and enhance it, with new public spaces, modern services and gathering places intended for residents and tourists. The new office thus forms part of a broader plan.

## Key facts Place: Canton of Ticino Result: 3 arrests Type: Shock Call Scam
The authorities of the Canton of Ticino have made three arrests related to a series of telephone scams based on the 'shock calls' method. This system of deception aims to psychologically destabilize the victim through sudden and alarming communications, prompting them to pay sums of money to solve alleged urgent problems or family emergencies.
### The operation of the network The investigation made it possible to identify those responsible who operated on the Ticino territory, using manipulation techniques to target vulnerable people. The detainees were arrested after a monitoring activity that revealed the structure of the gang and the way in which the victims were selected. The operation ended with the intervention of law enforcement who secured the suspects, disrupting the criminal activity that was affecting several residents and patrons of the region. ## Implications for those who live and work at the border Telephone scams represent a real risk for anyone who transits daily between Italy and Switzerland. Border crossers, who often operate checking accounts in both currencies and use international phone numbers, can become attractive targets for these criminal networks. The cross-border nature of many digital services makes it easier for fraudsters to disguise their identity or simulate calls from official institutions in the Canton of Ticino.
### Mobility risks Those who pass through crossings such as Brogeda or Chiasso and interact with different administrations may be more inclined to believe in calls that simulate urgent bureaucratic or fiscal problems. The use of technical terms related to work in Switzerland, such as source tax or G permit, could be used by criminals to give credibility to their story. ### The Tunnel Incident
An accident occurred around 5.15 pm on 13 October 2026 inside the Vedeggio-Cassarate gallery, in the direction of Lugano. The first image available shows a stationary car: the occupants have gotten off and are on the side of the road. The photograph has arrived at the newsroom and documents the scene in the early stages of the episode.
The source does not clarify at the moment if there are injured people. This is the only element reported on the possible consequences for those who were in the car and does not allow to add further details about their status.
The tunnel was closed and the blockade affected the two portals of the tunnel, where a snake of stacked cars formed. The closure occurred while traffic was supported by rush hour, with effects on the area surrounding the Lugano-Nord motorway exit.
The first picture returned by the news is therefore that of an accident within the connection to Lugano, followed by the suspension of transit and a rapid accumulation of vehicles. The information available concerns the stationary car, the occupants on the road and the road situation; however, the dynamics of the accident are not specified. ### The effect on the Lugano-Nord area
The closure was not confined within the gallery. The rush hour aggravated the consequences of the accident, causing heavy inconvenience to traffic in the area of the Lugano-Nord motorway exit. The stacked cars accumulated at the two portals, transforming the access to the connection into a long serpentine.
As the minutes passed, the repercussions began to be felt more and more towards the centre of Lugano. The problem described in the source therefore does not only concern the point where the accident occurred: the difficulty extended along the roadway that connects the exit area to the city.
Circulation in the city has been defined as very difficult and, in some areas, even paralysed. item.description: The vote on VAT for AVS is scheduled for November 29.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The vote on VAT for the AVS is set for November 29. - The proposed increase would bring VAT to 8,5%. - The 13th AVS pension costs 4-5 billion francs a year. - From 2028, the additional revenue would be approximately 1,5 billion per year.
## Key facts - Supporters → PS, Centro, Verdi, PEV and USS - Location of the announcement → Bern - VAT increase → +0,4 percentage points, up to 8,5% - First payment → December - Next outlook → AVS 2030 reform
On November 29, funding for the 13th AVS pension will go to a vote. In Bern, a broad alliance made up of PS, Centro, Verdi, PEV and USS presented the arguments in favor of an increase in VAT. The news report, bearing the Keystone-ATS byline, presents a common position: without a solid funding solution, the entire AVS risks running into difficulty.
For the cross-border commuter reader, the scope of the news is clear: it concerns AVS and pension funding. The source does not mention Canton Ticino, a G permit, LPP, LAMal, rebates, withholding tax, INPS, Brogeda, the new 2026 tax agreement or double taxation. These topics therefore cannot be cited as consequences described by the vote. To follow only the pension-related aspect, one can consult rendita AVS.
### The proposal on the table
The mechanism put forward by the alliance is an increase described as moderate: 0,4 percentage points in VAT, up to 8,5%. According to Samira Marti, co-president of the Socialist parliamentary group, adequately funding the 13th monthly payment through this measure would provide stability and security for pensions. The National Councillor from Basel-Landschaft also recalled that nine out of ten people receive more from the AVS than they pay in.
Centro, with its president Philipp Matthias Bregy, linked the vote to the AVS's financial sustainability. The 13th AVS pension entails additional annual costs of between 4 and 5 billion francs. The reserves, although still significant, are not unlimited. Moreover, the fund's assets are invested and generate returns that help finance the pensions: if the reserves fall, these returns also decline over the long term.
For this reason, Centro supports the compromise drawn up by parliament. From 2028, the measure should bring in about 1,5 billion francs more each year and slow the erosion of the reserves. Bregy ruled out, however, that the project could cover the funding needs on its own: in his assessment, further solutions will have to come with the AVS 2030 reform. The same alliance therefore presents a yes vote as a stabilization measure, not as the definitive financing of the AVS. ## What changes in the comparison
The practical point for those following the AVS from across the border is not to automatically attribute every issue related to working in Switzerland to the vote. The text makes it possible to separate the tax measure, the promised coverage and the AVS's financial outlook. These are three different levels, and the distinction prevents a political position from being turned into a rule that is already in force.
### Three levels to keep separate
The first level concerns VAT. Marti argues that food and medicines, described as essential goods, would not be affected by the moderate increase. Hence his conclusion: low and middle incomes would be protected. This is the alliance's wording; it is not an individual calculation for those who work across the border.
Regarding the relationship between costs and benefits, Léonore Porchet estimated that a person with an average income would pay about 85 francs more in VAT each year and, once reaching retirement age, would receive an additional pension of about 2000 francs per year. The vice-president of the Greens acknowledged that the tax system is proportionally more advantageous for higher incomes than an increase in wage contributions, adding, however, that it entails significant compensation. For a cross-border worker, this indication should be read as a political example provided by the source, not as a personal calculation: income, pension situation or other individual conditions are not specified.
The third level concerns timing. According to the alliance, a yes vote would slow the erosion of the reserves; in Bregy's words, a no vote would put the AVS and its beneficiaries at risk. The source does not describe an automatic outcome of the vote, but it also reports Pierre-Yves Maillard's accusation: UDC and PLR would be pursuing a destabilization strategy to push the AVS into the red and impose a higher retirement age on everyone. It is a political claim, not a separate fact.
Marc Jost adds a fourth argument: pensioners would also contribute through VAT, strengthening solidarity between generations. According to the Bernese national councillor, another choice would leave the bill to the children and grandchildren. The calcolatore fiscale can serve only for a personal reading of the figures, not to attribute different amounts to the source.

### A four-step timeline
For a cross-border worker who wants to get their bearings without adding extraneous information, the most cautious procedure is to turn the source into a brief timeline. No assumptions about the outcome are needed: the dates and figures stated by the supporters are enough.
1. Set the first reference point: November 29 is the date of the vote. The subject is not a generic reform, but the proposal to increase VAT intended to finance the 13th AVS pension payment.
2. Separate the decision from the payment. The 13th pension payment, wanted by the people through the USS popular initiative accepted in March 2024, will be paid for the first time in December. The source therefore describes two distinct moments: the vote on the financing and the first disbursement.
3. Write the exact figure next to the measure: +0,4 percentage points, up to 8,5%. Then record the two financial figures cited: the additional annual cost between 4 and 5 billion and additional revenue of approximately 1,5 billion per year from 2028. Do not present the latter as full coverage, because Bregy states the contrary.
4. Close the note with the stated limitation. The Centre supports the compromise, but admits that other solutions will be needed with the AVS 2030 reform. Next to it, note that UDC and PLR oppose the increase according to the report, while PS, Centre, Greens, PEV and USS support a yes vote. The positions remain attributed to their respective representatives.
This sequence helps avoid confusing the date of the vote with that of the payment and the expected revenue with the overall funding requirement. ### The proposal and its numbers
In Zurich, a proposal to restore the AVS without generally increasing the retirement age takes hold. The criterion would be different: to establish the exit from work, the years worked and the contributions paid would be counted, not only the achievement of an equal age for all.
For the border worker working in Switzerland, this is the part of the debate to follow: the source describes a possible change in the Swiss pension mechanism, but the political confrontation is still open. The proposal is supported by the bourgeois parties, while the left opposes it. The issue has entered into the stances on the AVS2030 reform, which is in preparation.
The idea comes from a concrete difference in careers. Those who carry out an apprenticeship can start paying contributions as early as 18 years old. Graduates often enter the workforce around the age of 25 or later. With the current rules, however, both reach the reference age of 65.
According to the model of the Centre Patronal, a Romanian employers' association, a full income would require 44 years of contributions. Based on this simulation, a skilled worker could retire at age 62, while a graduate sociologist would, for example, have to work until age 68. These are examples of the model, not a calendar valid for each worker.
According to a survey commissioned by the same organization, 72% of respondents rate the proposal very or quite positively.
However, several nodes remain. An early retirement would reduce pension payments and second-pillar benefits; changes to that system would also be needed to make up the difference. The debate also concerns loopholes, the contribution threshold, physically heavy or psychologically demanding professions and incomplete data on careers. The text therefore remains a proposal submitted for comparison, not a final decision. To follow the possible effect on the annuity, see approfondimento sulla rendita. ## The second pillar can change the outcome
### Early retirement is not neutral
For a cross-border worker who works in Switzerland, the practical question would not only be when work ends, but what pension remains after retirement. The proposal changes the first criterion, while the second pillar would follow a different logic: those who leave earlier pay fewer contributions to the pension fund and receive lower benefits. Any advantage of early retirement may therefore be accompanied by lower benefits in the second pillar, if the supplementary system is not modified.
The issue concerns the overall financial outcome. According to the model described, what matters above all is the average actual retirement age. If this rose, the mechanism could turn into an increase in the retirement age achieved through the back door. For Green national councillor Katharina Prelicz-Huber, everyone should know in advance when they will be able to retire, without depending on the course of their career. The left therefore prefers other measures to shore up the AVS.
There is also an opposite scenario. Even without changing the current average, people with high incomes could remain at work longer, pay contributions for longer and receive the pension for fewer years. According to the source, this effect could help finance the pensions of those who stop working earlier. It would not, however, be an individual guarantee: the outcome would depend on the actual average and the rules adopted.
The minimum threshold is another delicate point. If a minimum contribution were enough to accumulate a qualifying year, students could use it to fill gaps and bring retirement forward. A much higher threshold, such as the one proposed by the UDC, could instead risk penalizing those earning low wages or working part-time.
Defining the jobs that justify earlier retirement would also be complicated. The construction worker represents the most obvious physically demanding case, but there are occupations that are less strenuous physically yet involve strong psychological pressure or demanding hours. For the cross-border worker, the useful comparison therefore remains between years of contributions, second-pillar benefits and possible actual retirement age. A strumento per la rendita helps keep these three dimensions distinct.

### Four steps to avoid confusing assumptions with rules
The source does not describe a procedure already in force: the proposal emerges from positions taken on the AVS2030 reform, which is in preparation. For a cross-border worker, the most cautious way to read the issue is to separate the model's data from the rules currently in force. The analysis can be organized into four steps.
1. Reconstruct the beginning of your career. Note when you started working or paying contributions. The source's comparison starts from two different paths: an apprenticeship can lead to contributions at an earlier age, while a degree often precedes entry into work at a later stage.
2. Count the years of contributions as a variable separate from age. Use the requirement indicated by Centre Patronal for a full pension as a model parameter. Do not, however, treat the ages in the examples as personal thresholds: they concern two specific professional profiles within that simulation.
3. Check the effect on the second pillar. Early retirement would mean, according to the source, fewer contributions to the pension fund and lower benefits. This step cannot be separated from the debate on the overall pension.
4. Note the issues that are still open. The minimum threshold for making a contribution year valid, the UDC's proposal for a higher threshold, the possible penalization of low wages and part-time work, the classification of professions, and the collection of career data require answers before a definitive rule. The source also warns that complete data are currently lacking and that collecting them would take decades.
An additional check concerns the actual average retirement age, on which the model's financial outcome would depend. If the average rose, the mechanism could amount to an increase in the retirement age through the back door; if it remained at the current average, financing would also come from higher earners working longer. For the cross-border worker, the final comparison must therefore place years of contributions, the second pillar, and the system average side by side. ### The chronology of the three interventions
From 12 October, on the SS 34 in Cannobio, traffic is regulated alternating one-way to allow work on the tunnels. The construction site is being installed and, between 5 am and 9 pm, traffic is regulated by a traffic light or by mobile operators. From 21 October, however, the road will be closed every night, from 9 pm to 5 am.
For the replacement of the night connection, the notice of the Municipality cited by the M5S indicates four evening boat services between Cannero and Cannobio, in addition to one more ride of the Intra-Laveno ferry. According to the note, border workers, evening shift workers and people who return after dinner are the most exposed: the lake represents for them the only alternative and the availability of seats is limited.
At the bridge of Via San Giovanni Bosco, in Intra, the Municipality gave the green light to the executive project for seismic safety, worth 3.15 million. The commissioning of the works is now awaited. However, the M5S Vco territorial group asks how, for the entire duration of the construction site, hilly roads and any emergency connections to the hospital will be guaranteed.
Blessed Giovannina, after the resignation of the company that had been awarded the contract, the contract was terminated and the administration started a new negotiated procedure. The planned roundabout is worth about half a million euros. The M5S reports that a substantial part of citizens consider it useless and that those resources could be allocated, for example, to the arrangement of the embankment of the San Giovanni river. The times have slipped with respect to the initial schedule, but, according to the note, the construction site will still arrive at a vital junction for the entrance to Pallanza and Suna.
Over 800 citizens had signed the request to stop the work and to start a confrontation with the city, while all the minority groups asked for it to be set aside. Considering these three interventions together with those already open, the M5S Vco describes a "perfect storm" and points out the absence of a concrete plan to manage mobility. ### What travelers need to know
For a cross-border commuter, the distinction is between regulated traffic and a road closure. item.description: Salaries matter, but they alone do not determine the return.

## TL;DR - Salaries weigh heavily, but they do not determine the return on their own. - For a graduate-level job, salaries are 38% lower than in Zurich. - More than half of those who leave return within five years. - Between the ages of 25 and 35, around 300 people enter each year.
## Key facts - Event → morning at the Palazzo dei Congressi di Lugano - Organizers → Economic Division of Canton Ticino and City of Lugano - Wage differential → 38% lower than in the Zurich region - Returns → more than half of those who leave return within five years - 25-35 age group → around 300 people entering each year
At the Palazzo dei Congressi di Lugano, Monday's event organized by the Economic Division of Canton Ticino together with the City of Lugano examined the path of young people who leave the canton to pursue their education and often decide to return. The most unexpected result concerns pay: it influences the choice, but does not determine it on its own.
People used to speak of a brain drain. Today, in the language used during the meeting, they prefer to speak of talents on the move. People also return despite salary prospects that are lower than elsewhere in Switzerland. For a graduate-level job, the difference compared with the Zurich region is as much as 38% lower.
### Salary is part of the choice
Barbara Antonioli Mantegazzini, head of SUPSI's Center of Competence in Social Research, explained that income remains important, but can become secondary when three elements come into play: work-life balance, the possibility of a more stable and permanent contract, and consistency between the skills acquired, the studies completed and the job found. These criteria are joined by the desire to move closer again to family or friends, as well as motivations related to the climate and cuisine.
The discussion also touched on Ticino's ability to bring back young people educated outside the canton. Lorenzo Barisone, who follows the statistical data of the City of Lugano, reported improvements in the return of young people in education. The destination is not limited to other cantons, however: the source indicates a majority heading abroad and to Italy, where Ticino's salary advantage remains competitive.
Stefano Rizzi, director of the Economic Division of Canton Ticino, indicated another figure: more than half of the young people who leave return after just five years. The stated goal is to further increase returns. In the 25-35 age group, taking immigration into account, the balance records an average inflow into Ticino of around 300 people per year. These are people who arrive, study and also find work. For Rizzi, the issue comes down to the ability to match supply and demand and to work on the area's attractive features. Companies, he emphasized, also have a responsibility. The topic can be explored further through the aziende che assumono. ## The comparison that matters to those who work in Ticino
For those who live near the border and work in Ticino, the message can also be read as a practical rule: it is not enough to place two salaries side by side. The source suggests a broader criterion: a lower salary than in Zurich can be evaluated together with the quality of the work and the possibility of establishing a longer-term presence.
### Three levels to compare
The pay gap remains evident: for a graduate-level job, the salary in Ticino is 38% lower than in the Zurich region, but, although it is not decisive on its own, it is not irrelevant. Other factors in the choice may include work-life balance, the possibility of a stable contract, and the fit between the skills one has, one's educational path and the work performed.
This perspective also changes how a return is viewed. For those who are still in education, the inclination to move may emerge almost immediately after their studies. For those already in another canton, by contrast, an attraction policy must contend with different motivations. The distinction is not relevant only to policymakers: it also helps those considering an offer understand what question they are asking themselves: whether to stay, leave or return.
Another comparison concerns destinations. The other cantons are not the only destinations for young people from Ticino; the source indicates that a majority head abroad and to Italy. For this part of the movement, Ticino's salary advantage is described as remaining competitive. For the cross-border worker, this passage is an invitation not to confuse the comparison with Zurich with the comparison with Italy: these are different routes, and the source presents them separately.
For the cross-border worker, this perspective concerns the professional choice in Canton Ticino and should be kept separate from the matters of permit G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax and double taxation. To explore the available offering, the starting point remains annunci di lavoro, to be read together with the duties and contractual stability indicated.
