## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## A practical procedure for assessing a return
The source does not provide a single formula, but it does make it possible to construct a decision sequence without focusing solely on salary. For a cross-border worker interested in a job in Ticino, the steps can be ordered as follows.
### Four steps
1. Establish the trajectory. Ask yourself whether you are choosing your first position after completing your education or returning from another canton, abroad or Italy. The distinction is decisive because the propensity to move emerges almost immediately after the training period, whereas those who are already outside Ticino have different motivations.
2. Isolate the salary comparison. Use the available figure as a reference: for a graduate position, the indicated Ticino prospect is 38% lower than in the Zurich region. The figure serves to measure the gap, not to close the discussion. The choice remains open to the other elements mentioned during the morning.
3. Assess the content of the offer. Before deciding, focus on the balance between private and professional life, the possibility of a stable permanent contract, and the consistency between skills, studies and the work carried out. According to Barbara Antonioli Mantegazzini, these are the three points that can make the salary dimension secondary.
4. Broaden the horizon. Consider reconnecting with family and friends, the climate and the cuisine, then look at the five-year horizon: the data presented indicate that more than half of the young people who leave return within that period. It is a way of viewing the return as a trajectory, not as an isolated choice.
The sequence also helps distinguish what depends on the individual from what depends on the market. On the one hand there are skills, expectations and ties; on the other, Ticino’s and companies’ ability to match supply and demand. For those considering a change, the final check consists of comparing the salary with the actual work and the promised stability, without leaving either of the two terms out of consideration. ## TL;DR - Clash between two cars on state road 69 in Brezzo di Bedero - Incident around 6 am on Tuesday 13 October - First aid taken off from Como for a seriously injured person - Queues and critical issues still reported at 7.30 am

Brezzo di Bedero, Tuesday 13 October. Around 6 in the morning two cars collided on state road 69, the road that runs along the upper Lake Maggiore. The accident was serious enough to require the intervention of the air ambulance, which flew from Como, to rescue at least one person in serious condition.
The time slot coincides with the moment in which the traffic in the area has already awakened. For the reader who travels along this axis, the reference to keep in mind is therefore the combination between the state road 69, the town of Brezzo di Bedero and the Zenna passage.
Among those involved is a 22-year-old young man. The source does not clarify whether he was the injured person transported by helicopter: the identity of the person transferred by helicopter is not indicated. There is no other information on the dynamics other than the involvement of the two cars.
### Interventions and traffic
In addition to the helicopter that left Como, two ambulances from Luino and Cunardo and the medical vehicle from Varese arrived on site. The Fire Brigade and the Carabinieri also intervened. The news reports serious conditions for at least one person, but does not add other medical details on the accident.
The consequences on traffic were manifested by queues in the area of ​​the accident. The flow gradually dissipated with the passage of time; at 7.30, however, there were still some road problems. item.title: The poker room at Casinò Admiral in Mendrisio is closing
item.description: The poker room at Casinò Admiral closes on November 30 The project had started on January 1, 2022 Redeployment is planned for the 15 employees
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The poker room at Casinò Admiral closes on November 30 - The project began on January 1st, 2022 - Redeployment and training are planned for the 15 collaborators - Only The Barracudas will take place from November 19 to 29
## Key facts - Location → Casinò Admiral di Mendrisio - Closing → November 30 - Project launch → January 1, 2022 - Staff involved → 15 - Person in charge → Cristiano Ruiu - Final tournament → Only The Barracudas - Tournament dates → November 19-29 - Lombard clientele → approximately 85% of clientele
On November 30, the poker room at Casinò Admiral di Mendrisio will cease operations, bringing an end to a project that has attracted enthusiasts from across the border for five years. The room had helped raise the casino’s profile, and news of the closure, widely discussed on social media, was confirmed by Cristiano Ruiu, marketing, poker and product development manager at Casinò Admiral.
Ruiu explained that the initiative began on January 1, 2022, while the pandemic was still ongoing, with the aim of revitalizing the casino. At the time, he recalled, Campione, a long-standing poker institution in the area, had not yet reopened. In his view, after five full years, the room has achieved its objectives.
### The project and its assessment
The poker room expanded its clientele and gave Casinò Admiral visibility beyond the regional borders. The marketing manager attributed this result mainly to tournaments, which gave players visibility and generated articles in Italy, Switzerland and throughout Europe.
Ruiu gave a positive assessment of the experience, describing it as very good and positive, and described the closure as the natural conclusion of a journey. In his view, it is not a sinking ship, but rather a cruise ship that has reached port after completing its journey.
The manager’s wording confirms the November 30 shutdown without erasing the role played by the room during its years of operation. The project began during a particular period, when the pandemic was still ongoing and Casinò di Campione d'Italia had not reopened. Against that backdrop, Admiral had chosen to focus on poker to attract enthusiasts and increase its visibility.
The news therefore concerns a specific facility of Casinò Admiral di Mendrisio and not the end of the casino’s operations as a whole. Ruiu spoke about the poker room and its results, explaining that the project had achieved its goals after five full years. The room will nevertheless remain operational until the announced date, when operations will cease. ## The 15 employees and the economic reasons
The closure of the poker room raises the question of the future of the 15 employees who work there. Cristiano Ruiu reported that the announcement came in September, first to the staff committee and only afterward to the people directly concerned. The announcement preceded the end of operations, set for November 30.
ACE Swiss Holding, a sister company of Novomatic, has provided several options for the staff. Employees can be reassigned to other areas of the company, pursue training and retraining programs, or be transferred to another casino in the group. The source does not present a single solution for everyone, but describes a range of internal and group-wide options.
Ruiu emphasized the difference from a scenario in which the department would simply have been closed, leaving everyone without a job. In Admiral's case, however, he spoke of a company that had provided solutions for all the employees involved. The employment issue thus remains tied to the possibilities of reassignment, training, retraining and transfer indicated by the company.
### Campione is not the cause
The resumption of operations at Casinò di Campione d'Italia could suggest that competition for the poker room in Mendrisio has intensified. Ruiu, however, ruled out this being the reason for the closure. In his view, the room had been opened to fill the void created by the bankruptcy of the company operating the casino and to respond to market demand.
This interpretation therefore rules out the possibility that the shutdown is due to Campione's reopening. The manager pointed to other factors: gaming taxes, among the highest in Switzerland, which squeeze an already limited profit margin, and staffing costs.
### The issue of daily tournaments
The burden of the cost structure makes a schedule of daily tournaments impractical. Ruiu noted that, unlike Mendrisio, the other Swiss casinos do not offer tournaments every day because the cost-benefit ratio is difficult to sustain.
His assessment of poker remains positive, however. Ruiu considers it an excellent marketing tool, but one to be used for a limited period, as was done at Casinò Admiral. The room therefore served a promotional and visibility function, while the continuation of daily tournaments must contend with costs, gaming taxes and staffing.
The manager's account separates two aspects: on the one hand, the poker room's contribution to the casino's profile, and on the other, the economic sustainability of a daily schedule. The closure is thus attributed to the end of a project and a cost structure that is difficult to maintain, not to the reopening of Casinò di Campione d'Italia. ## Ruiu remains in casino marketing
The closure of the poker room does not mark Cristiano Ruiu's exit from the sector. Casino marketing has been his profession for eleven years, across Campione, Lugano and Mendrisio, and he has said he wants to continue along this path.
In his approach, poker was one of the elements of Casinò Admiral's marketing strategy. The aim was to attract players without allocating resources to visitors outside the target audience. Ruiu distinguished between promotions designed for players and events aimed at other audiences: to bring players to the casino, he cited promotions involving chips or slot vouchers; an event with a sommelier, by contrast, would attract wine enthusiasts rather than players.
Alongside his work in casinos, Ruiu has collaborated with Telelombardia for 28 years and now considers this activity a hobby. The public profile he built in nearby Lombardy has also been useful to him in his work in Mendrisio, a casino frequented by many customers from Lombardy.
The source puts the proportion of Casinò Admiral's clientele from Lombardy at approximately 85%. Ruiu said he had tried to put his public profile at the service of the company he works for. The reference to Lombardy therefore concerns both his television career and the origin of a very substantial portion of the casino's clientele.
Recently, Ruiu also appeared as a commentator on RSI. His appearances, however, were sporadic and linked to the football World Cup. It is therefore not presented as a new regular activity, but as an occasional contribution connected to that sporting event.
### The final tournament
Before the shutdown, the poker room at Admiral in Mendrisio has scheduled the final event in its operating history: Only The Barracudas. The final tournament will take place from November 19 to 29, so it will precede by a few days the closure of operations scheduled for November 30.
Ruiu invited the public to attend an event he considers historic. Whoever wins the tournament will be the last player to win a poker competition at Casinò di Mendrisio. The event will bring the project begun on January 1st, 2022, and the poker room's schedule to a close before operations conclude.
For enthusiasts, the dates given are November 19-29. For the 15 collaborators, however, the next step remains tied to the possibilities for redeployment, training, retraining or transfer already planned by ACE Swiss Holding within the company or group. For his part, Ruiu will continue working in casino marketing, building on the experience gained in Campione, Lugano and Mendrisio.

On Thursday 15 October, Materia Spazio Libero in Castronno will host the presentation of Varese città del Cavolo, the first festival of Varese brassicas. The evening has been conceived as a special event for the hub: in addition to the cultural discussion, it includes a themed dinner in the agora.
The initiative stems from a very common presence in the fields and vegetable gardens of the Varese area. Cabbage, in its various forms, is everywhere: from head cabbage to black cabbage, including savoy cabbage and pak choi, Chinese cabbage. This very widespread presence, often observed without being recognized, led Franca Formenti to envision a festival dedicated to the area's brassicas.
The project also plays on the double meaning of the word cavolo, but the evening in Castronno presents it as a serious effort to promote the produce. The point is not merely to talk about a vegetable: it is to highlight what is already grown, cooked and served in the Varese area. For this reason, alongside the cultural segment, the format includes the convivial moment of dinner.
### A presentation dedicated to the local supply chain
The first edition puts growers, restaurateurs and florists at the centre, with the aim of drawing attention to vegetable gardens, flowers and activities connected to food. The evening at Materia serves to present the project and connect the discussion of brassicas with their tangible presence in fields and menus.
It is not presented as a simple celebration of cabbage. The deliberately ironic name attracts attention, while the content concerns cultivation, food and dining, areas that will be addressed with various guests. The chosen format therefore combines the discussion with a dinner prepared around the initiative's theme.
For the Castronno hub, this is also a new development in its event programming, because the evening combines the cultural segment with a convivial moment in the agora. It will be the festival's most cultural moment, while the other events and participating activities are listed on the initiative's official website. ## From observing the fields to expert verification
For two years Franca Formenti observed gardens and countryside in the Varese area, finding cabbages, savoy cabbages, black cabbage and numerous other species throughout the area. Her intuition was strengthened when a German association chose cabbage as “vegetable of the year”.
From there, discussions with nursery growers and farmers began. Formenti found fields full of brassicas and proposed a festival to highlight what she called a hidden excellence. According to the creator's account, cultivation already exists, but it is not talked about enough.
> Varese is at the forefront, and no one talks about it.
The first expert brought in was agronomist Luciano Riva. Formenti showed him the project to verify its validity and received a positive assessment. Riva also sent her an in-depth text, published on the festival's official website. His assessment confirmed Varese's suitability for growing brassicas and supported the launch of the initiative.
### The expertise brought together at Materia
Luciano Riva, agronomist and director of the magazine Habitat Ambiente, will be one of the main participants in the event, together with Rolando Saccucci, fiduciary of Slow Food's Varese chapter, and Dr. Marta Maugeri, a medical nutritionist.
The agricultural side will be represented by Luisa Broggini and Camilla Crugnola of OrtoBroggini. The restaurant sector, meanwhile, will be represented by Gianni Malnati and Elena Spasciani from the pizzeria Così com'è, which is taking part in the initiative. The mix of guests brings together at the same event the perspectives of agronomy and nutrition, agricultural production, and culinary experience.
According to Formenti, the purpose of the program is to show that this is not merely a festival devoted to cabbage. The evening aims to acknowledge the work already being done in Varese around brassicas, from field to table, with the contribution of those who grow them, study them, explore their benefits, or include them in their own menus. ## Events after the presentation
The evening of October 15 will be the most cultural moment, but the festival will continue with other activities listed on the official website. Various businesses have joined, from farm stays to restaurants and growers, offering cabbage-based dishes on their menus.
The calendar also includes an event scheduled for October 28 at Zona Franca. It is an aperitif dinner with a nutritionist, designed to explore the beneficial effects of cabbage. The initiative thus takes the subject beyond cultivation alone and connects it to food, with a meeting led by Dr. Marta Maugeri.
A fermentation workshop is also scheduled between November 1 and 2. The technique is described as one of the most important methods for preserving cabbages and represents another way to address the subject of brassicas, after the cultural evening and the offerings of participating establishments.
### The options for the Castronno evening
Two participation options are available for the event at Materia. You can book the full evening, with dinner in the agora, or just the cultural portion. The source provides a link for choosing either option and confirming your place.
The presentation also marks Franca Formenti's first public appearance as Studio Food Power, the studio founded with the aim of communicating food differently. Formenti explained that she has been involved in activism and art since 2007 and has noticed that, in the world of communication, languages already used twenty years ago are still being employed.
For her, Materia's invitation represents validation of the new studio. The evening, together with the subsequent events, thus becomes the first public journey of a project that starts with the cabbages found in the fields of Varesotto and brings them into meetings, menus, nutrition and preservation techniques.

## TL;DR - Fabio De Luigi returns to the theater after twenty-five years - BIOL – In Carne e Ossa opens the season in Varese - The Varese stop is the third of the tour - More than 1000 people at Teatro Intred
## Key facts - Entertainment → BIOL – In the flesh - Protagonist → Fabio De Luigi - Place → Varese Theatre, Piazza Repubblica - Stage → third of the tour - Audience → over 1000 people - Authors → Fabio De Luigi and Paolo Cananzi - Production → Live Nation
### The debut of the tour Fabio De Luigi officially opened the new theatrical season of the Teatro di Varese with BIOL – In Carne e Ossa, the work that marks the return of the Romagna actor to the stage after twenty-five years away from the theatre. The hall in Piazza Repubblica thus inaugurated the program with an evening dedicated to an artist who, after a long journey especially in cinema and television, has chosen to re-establish a direct relationship with the public.
Varese was the third overall stop on the tour, arriving immediately before the Milanese appointment. The audience responded with important numbers: the Intred theater welcomed over 1000 people. The live return therefore opened in a room filled with the public and in a season that had just started.
The show was written together with Paolo Cananzi and produced by Live Nation. Its structure brings together monologues, stories, improvisations and more intimate ideas. The result takes up De Luigi's comic and narrative tone without separating the personal story from entertainment.
At the center remains the transition from cinema and television to the stage. After twenty-five years of absence, De Luigi has resumed the tour with a work that the source describes as a reconnection of ties with the theater audience. The Varese event thus combined the opening of the program and the actor's theatrical restart.
Even the title finds a reference in the actor's memory. At the origin of the show lies a childhood memory: the detergent with the Dutch girl peeking out of the porthole of a washing machine. The familiar detail accompanies a project built not only on already known characters, but also on more personal stories and passages.
The debut in Varese brought to the stage De Luigi's theatrical restart and the opening of the program of the theater in Piazza Repubblica. The stage preceded Milan and presented the live format of BIOL – In Carne e Ossa to the public, between narration, comedy and improvisation. ## A career retrospective without nostalgia
### Two recognizable returns The evening began in a festive mood. The audience at Teatro di Varese greeted De Luigi with a spontaneous chorus of “Happy birthday,” dedicated to the occasion the actor had celebrated the previous day. The tribute gave the evening a festive opening and marked the first contact between the actor and the Varese audience.
The career retrospective was carefully calibrated. The performance avoided the risk of turning into a mere parade of old crowd-pleasers and allowed only two nostalgic interludes. They were placed at two clearly defined points, the opening and the closing, while the rest adopted a more conversational and narrative tone.
At the beginning, the inevitable reference to Ingegner Cane returned. The character was the first recognizable nod to one part of the actor’s career, without turning the entire show into a sequence of reprises. The memory thus remained present, but concentrated in one precise moment of the evening.
In closing, Olmo reappeared, with his irreverent romanticism and the celebrated Sei una merda. The finale was enriched by a vocal surprise: Olmo was introduced by Marco Mengoni’s voice, remembered as a fan of his predecessor and his extraordinary successes. The reference gave the conclusion a different form from the opening, while nevertheless maintaining the same thread with De Luigi’s artistic past.
Between the two moments, the show maintained a polite and pleasant tone, with an intimate and familiar atmosphere. The set design remained minimalist, but not without impact. The inflatable dolphin and the little plush giraffe were the most prominent stage elements: the dolphin’s movement seemed random, but was actually carefully choreographed like that of a true co-star.
The choice to limit the nostalgic callbacks left room for anecdotes, stories, and improvisations. The audience thus encountered both familiar references and a more intimate narrative, within a balance that avoided reducing the return to the theater to a mere celebration of the past. ## Piadina, jokes and the local area
### The show beyond the script Amid hilarious anecdotes and moments of live entertainment, one of the evening’s most original moments came in the form of the onstage cooking demonstration. De Luigi rolled out a Romagna piadina, demonstrating seasoned skill, and then tossed it directly into the audience. The preparation thus became part of the entertainment and brought to the center of the room an element connected to his Romagna roots.
The rapport with the audience also took shape through jokes about the people of Como. The reference was delivered with a certain crowd-pleasing spirit and a knowledge of the area that the audience especially appreciated. The comedy therefore did not remain separate from the setting of the evening: it also used references recognizable to those listening from the province of Varese and nearby areas.
The piadina tossed among the spectators, the improvisations, and the local jokes gave the performance a direct, immediate feel. They are different moments, but all belong to the same dimension of live entertainment described in the report: not just monologues, but also onstage action and exchanges with the audience.
The connection with the province of Varese emerged even more concretely at the end of the show. De Luigi offered special thanks to the historic Caffè Teatro di Verghera di Samarate, a venue that launched many leading figures in Italian comedy. The actor followed the acknowledgment with the clarification “But not me,” thereby also recalling his own particular relationship with that place.
Caffè Teatro was not mentioned solely as a reference point for Italian comedy. It also hosted part of the rehearsals for this show. The final thanks therefore linked the evening open to the public with a phase of the preparatory work carried out in the Varese area.
The closing highlighted precisely this dual connection: on the one hand, the relationship built onstage with the audience; on the other, the reference to a place in the province where part of the rehearsals took place. For the opening evening of Teatro di Varese, the local area entered the story through comedy, the piadina, jokes about the people of Como, and the tribute to Caffè Teatro di Verghera di Samarate.

## TL;DR - Green Range cares for the meadow of Franco Ossola in 2026/2027 - Municipal deed: 12 October 2026 - 7% discount on auction prices - Amount: 38,114.13 euros plus VAT
## Key facts - What → ordinary maintenance of grassy areas - Where → Franco Ossola stadium, Masnago - Who → Gamma Verde S.r.l., Mariano Comense - Act → managerial determination number 1400 - Date → October 12, 2026 - Procedure → Sintel, with a 7% discount - Amount → 38,114.13 euros plus VAT - Total → approximately 46,500 euros on the 2026-2027 municipal budget
### The assignment for the 2026/2027 season Management determination number 1400 of 12 October 2026 puts in black and white the decision of the Municipality of Varese for the care of the grassy areas of the Franco Ossola stadium, in the Masnago facility. The Public Works Area approved the project and entrusted the ordinary maintenance service to Gamma Verde S.r.l. by Mariano Comense.
The assignment concerns the 2026/2027 season and is part of the temporary management of maintenance of the stadium's greenery. The perimeter of the contract is that of the grassy areas of the facility, with ordinary care intended to support the sporting activity indicated in the municipal documentation.
The award took place through the Sintel electronic procedure. The selected company offered a 7% discount on the starting auction prices. The value of the assignment amounts to 38,114.13 euros plus VAT, while the overall total indicated in the 2026-2027 municipal budget is approximately 46,500 euros.
The provision therefore defines both the operator in charge and the economic dimension of the service. Gamma Verde, based in Mariano Comense, enters into the management of the stadium's turf for the indicated season, on the basis of a project approved by the municipal administration.
The act concerns ordinary maintenance and does not present the assignment as a complete management of the entire sports complex. Lawn care is organized through a specific assignment, with a duration linked to the 2026/2027 season and with an amount included in the accounts of the Municipality of Varese. ### The field and the sports calendar The reason for the intervention starts from the characteristics of the Masnago stadium. The main pitch of the Franco Ossola is in natural grass and, according to the documentation referred to in the source, must maintain a suitable standard together with the surrounding areas. Maintenance therefore concerns not only the surface used for the races, but also the grassy spaces connected to the plant.
The purpose indicated is to allow the regular performance of the 15 home matches of the "City of Varese" Sports Association. The calendar reported in the note inserted in the praetorian register places the meetings between October 11, 2026 and April 25, 2027. The team is committed to the Serie D championship, Group D.
The reference to internal tenders gives a concrete measure of the administrative need. The maintenance of the natural terrain is connected to a sports program already indicated in the documentation, with a precise time frame and with the aim of maintaining the field in the conditions required for the matches scheduled in Masnago.
In the note of the praetorian register appears the name of the Sports Association "City of Varese". The source specifies that, for some years, the club has been called Varese Football Club. The two indications are reported in the same information framework: on the one hand the name used in the administrative note, on the other the name of the company indicated by the editorial staff.
The calendar ### A still provisional management The technical report from the procedure manager clarifies the criterion chosen to organize the care of the stadium. The maintenance of the Franco Ossola is decoupled from the general city greenery contract: the grassy areas of the Masnago facility therefore follow a separate assignment compared to the overall management of the municipal greenery.
This transition is linked to the temporary nature of the solution. The care of the stadium is maintained through the assignment for the 2026/2027 season, while the future of the entire sports complex remains linked to a possible takeover by a concession company for the structure or to future structural redevelopment interventions.
The distinction indicated in the technical report separates the immediate issue of ordinary maintenance from the broader framework of the facility's management. On one hand, there is the service entrusted to Gamma Verde for the grassy areas; on the other, the prospect of a concession company or structural interventions on the entire sports complex remains open.
The municipal administration has thus approved a project limited to the lawn and green surfaces, without including it in the general city greenery contract. The choice allows for the accompaniment of the sports season indicated in the documentation, keeping the service intended for the stadium separate.

## TL;DR
- VBS launches the third edition of Inclusive Minibasket - Donations doubled by the Foundation from October 1 to October 31 - Training sessions every Tuesday at the Pellico Gym in Varese
## Key facts
- Organizer → SSD Varese Basket School - Project → «Inclusive Minibasket» - Training sessions → Tuesday, 16:15-17:15, Pellico Gym - Fundraiser → donations doubled throughout October - Event → «Uniform Party», October 17, Falaschi Gym
### The project in the gym
In the month of philanthropy, SSD Varese Basket School (VBS) presents in Varese, for the third consecutive year, a new edition of the «Inclusive Minibasket» project. The initiative uses sport to promote inclusion and involves children with and without disabilities.
The stated goal is to offer a concrete opportunity to play together, have fun and build friendships. The project brings together children with and without disabilities in the same opportunity to play, with a program designed to make minibasket accessible to everyone.
The sessions are scheduled every Tuesday afternoon, from 16:15 to 17:15, at the Pellico Gym in Varese. For one hour, the gym becomes a space where sport is presented as accessible and open to everyone. The program is led by a qualified team of VBS coaches, who support the children on the court.
The initiative has a twofold impact. Children with disabilities develop social, motor and cognitive skills; their teammates learn to put themselves out there and adapt the rules so that no one is left out. Mutual respect is thus learned during the activity, through shared experience on the court.
The setting is calm and welcoming. Every young athlete sees their abilities recognized and receives support in situations of greater vulnerability. For VBS, minibasket goes beyond a simple sport: it represents an opportunity to create bonds, challenge their own limits and experience a positive relationship with themselves and others.
The project's value is linked to the possibility of sharing sports practice and recognizing abilities and vulnerabilities without leaving anyone behind. Throughout the program, the dimension of play remains connected to growth and the building of relationships, according to an initiative aimed at all young athletes. ### Resources for keeping the program running
The financial support is organized through the campaign «30 days to donate». The initiative was created in collaboration with the Fondazione Comunitaria del Varesotto and covers the entire month of October: from October 1 to October 31, all donations intended for the «Inclusive Minibasket» are doubled by the Foundation.
The arrangement connects each contribution received during the stated period to concrete support for the project. The funds raised are used to cover expenses related to qualified educational staff, the purchase of sports equipment, and gym rentals. These are essential costs for carrying out the activity, which registration fees alone cannot cover.
The fundraising therefore relates to the people who take part in the program, the equipment used during the activity, and the spaces where training sessions can take place. The doubling provided by the Foundation applies to donations received during the campaign period and strengthens the support directed toward VBS's project.
In its message to the community, VBS also describes even the smallest donation as a strong sign of participation and closeness. The contribution is presented as a form of support for an activity that requires qualified staff, sports equipment, and gyms, in addition to the resources obtained through registration fees.
A mother's testimony also helps explain the meaning of the activity, linking the everyday act of training to the dignity accorded to every person:
> «During VBS's Inclusive Minibasket training sessions, holding hands takes on a special meaning: it can restore dignity and recognition to every person, whatever their circumstances»
The testimony links training to the recognition of the dignity and importance of every person, regardless of the circumstances in which they live. The mother's perspective adds to the presentation of the project a response directly linked to the experience of VBS's Inclusive Minibasket. ### The morning at Palestra Falaschi
The project will be celebrated at a public event, during which it will be possible to learn more about it up close. The «Uniform Day» will be held on Saturday, October 17, from 10:00 to 12:00, at Palestra Falaschi in Valle Olona, at Piazza don L. Gabbani, 1, in Varese.
The morning will begin with a segment dedicated to the athletes: all participants will receive a shirt and shorts. A practical demonstration of the inclusive activity is scheduled for around 11. The event will also help promote the fundraising campaign by linking the distribution of the uniform, the on-court trial and support for the project.
The stated schedule brings the activities announced for the Uniform Day together into two hours. It starts at 10 and ends at 12; the demonstration is scheduled for around 11. The Valle Olona venue will be the location identified by VBS to provide an up-close look at this initiative and present the inclusive activity.
### How to support Minibasket Inclusivo
The donation can be made online through the dedicated page on the Fondazione Comunitaria del Varesotto website. Bank transfer is also possible, payable to Fondazione Comunitaria del Varesotto Ente Filantropico, with IBAN IT87 N032 3901 6006 7000 1966 911. The payment reference should state «Minibasket Inclusivo».
Another option is scanning the QR Code included in the campaign materials. The listed options therefore include the online page, the bank transfer and the code associated with the materials distributed for the fundraising campaign.
For contacts and information, SSD Varese Basket School is listed. The contact is the email address progetti@varesebasketschool.it, provided alongside the donation methods and the October 17 event for information about the project and the campaign.

item.description: Two years' imprisonment for the Local Police officer The footage rules out the reported assault 5mila euro in provisional damages for the municipality More than 9mila euro
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two years' imprisonment for the Local Police officer - Footage rules out the reported assault - 5mila euro in provisional damages for the Municipality - Over 9mila euro in legal costs
## Key facts - Defendant → G.F., officer with the Busto Arsizio Local Police - Date of the events → February 1, 2023 - Location → via Travelli, Busto Arsizio - Decision → sentence of two years in prison - Offenses → simulation of a crime, causing public alarm, ideological falsification and fraud - Provisional compensation → 5mila euro to the Municipality - Legal costs → over 9mila euro
In July, the Court of Appeal sentenced G.F., an officer with the Busto Arsizio Local Police, to two years in prison, after the Busto Arsizio Court had acquitted him at first instance. The filed grounds set out a different reconstruction of the morning of February 1, 2023, when the man had reported an assault on via Travelli.
According to his account, the officer was carrying out a duty alone in the restricted traffic zone. He reported being pushed from behind by two strangers and described two young men wearing different jackets, one orange and one light-colored. The report led to the deployment of several Local Police patrols, also involving the State Police. The officer was taken to hospital and discharged with a prognosis of ten days.
The incident attracted the city’s attention and also involved the Municipality of Busto Arsizio, which joined the proceedings as a civil party. In the Court’s view, G.F. was responsible for several offenses: simulation of a crime, causing public alarm, ideological falsification and fraud. The administration was awarded 5mila euro in provisional compensation, plus more than 9mila euro in legal costs.
### The images at the center of the ruling
The Court gave particular weight to private recordings collected along the officer’s route, between via Carlo, via Sant'Ambrogio and via Travelli. The footage came from a couple of shops and a bank: some systems recorded continuously, while others were activated by movement.
None of the images showed the two alleged attackers. Instead, the recordings deemed decisive showed the officer alone: at one point he approached a wall and deliberately struck it with a knee; other sequences showed him rubbing his cheek and other parts of his body against a wall or a column.
At first instance, the Court had described those gestures as “bizarre,” but considered them insufficient to prove that the man had deliberately inflicted the injuries on himself. The same decision also considered the presence of a blind spot plausible. After reexamining the footage and renewing part of the evidentiary proceedings, the Court of Appeal instead found the uncovered area too small: the arrival, push and fall could not have occurred without at least part of the action or body appearing in the images. The theory involving the gates was also ruled out, because the bank’s continuous recording showed them always closed during the interval in question. The source describes local criminal proceedings: its connection with the audience of Frontaliere Ticino is territorial, not related to a change in cross-border work rules. ### Comparison between the two levels of jurisdiction
| Element | First instance | Court of Appeal | |---|---|---| | Gestures captured | «bizarre», insufficient | Assessed across all the footage | | Blind spot | Deemed plausible | Space too limited | | Outcome | Acquittal | Two years' imprisonment |
The most relevant point is not merely that no camera showed the two men. The Court based its reasoning on all the recordings, the size of the uncovered area and the continuity of the bank's system. The conclusion stems from comparing what should have appeared with what the images actually show: in the judges' view, the reported sequence of events could not have remained entirely out of frame.
The second level concerns causing a false alarm. The call to the Control Center had focused patrols on the search for the two men described and had also involved the State Police. The searches also extended to other areas of Busto Arsizio and Saronno station, but produced no results and involved a considerable number of working hours. For the Court, resources intended for public services were thus directed toward people who had not committed any assault.
The third level concerns contradictions in the defendant's version. G.F. had said that he could not identify the precise location of the assault and that he had associated two people seen running afterward with the incident, without being certain that they were the perpetrators. He had also denied injuring himself against the wall, explaining those movements as simply bracing himself after a shock. The Court deemed this explanation incompatible with the behavior captured on video.
